mainEntity.name: Do I need a chief-of-staff AI assistant, or am I overcomplicating a simple business workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text: A chief-of-staff-style assistant can be useful when you have several recurring projects, need consolidated updates, or keep losing track of which assistant owns each task. It is unnecessary for a single workflow that one assistant can complete with a clear checklist. The central assistant should route requests, maintain priorities, identify blocked work, and ask for owner decisions—not make every strategic decision itself. Create a task board with status, owner, next action, dependency, and approval state. Run My AI Biz’s resource examples include chief-of-staff coordination, but the focused starting recommendation is to build and use one relevant assistant before expanding.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use one when you have multiple projects, recurring handoffs, or a need for consolidated status updates. Skip it for a single straightforward task. Its role should be routing, tracking, and escalation—not replacing your business judgment.
